audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0-3 of the level chart disagreed across layers: content win[0..3] read 'Lux' (matching packet.levelChart) while full-layer phases[0..3].side all read 'Skill'. Worse, phases[5].why and phases[6].why both described LUX winning those stages while phases[5].side and phases[6].side read 'Vladimir'.
audit.why: Vladimir has no dash and both Transfusion and Tides of Blood stop at 600, against Lux's 1100 E and 1175 Q — levels 1-5 are hers on range and on his health-cost trading. From his first item Crimson Pact (30 bonus HP = 1 AP, 1 AP = 1.6 HP) converts every health item into damage, and Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetability negates the single commit Lux gets per cycle.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side moved to 'Lux' with ratings and whys rewritten in the same proposal; phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to describe VLADIMIR winning, matching the sides already on disk. No content win[N] edit is proposed because win[0..3] already read 'Lux' and win[5]/win[6] already read 'Vladimir' — a before==after edit would be refused. All seven rows agree across layers after application.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes and the phase whys described Lux's spikes only and never named Vladimir's, which is the reason the lane flips.
audit.why: Vladimir's spike is not an ability rank, it is Crimson Pact: his first big health/AP item converts both ways, so poke that mattered at level 5 stops sticking. Lux's spikes stay Lost Chapter, level 6 (Final Spark 60s at rank 1) and Luden's.
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes, phases[5].why, phases[6].why, enemyWin and breakdown.carry now name Crimson Pact as the flip point.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive interactions were absent: Sanguine Pool's untargetability eating a committed combo, and the fact that Vladimir's whole kit is health-costed and mana-free.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 2 seconds untargetable on 28/25/22/19/16s at 350 range and 0 cost. Transfusion is 9/7.9/6.8/5.7/4.6s, 600 range, 0 cost, and heals off minions as well as champions. Tides of Blood is 13/11/9/7/5s at 600 and costs his own health. Hemoplague is a flat 120s at 625, amplifies damage taken and heals him per champion hit. Lux answers with Q 10s/1175 root, E 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s at 1100, W 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, R 60/50/40s at 3340. The lane is decided by whether Lux's commit lands on the 20+ seconds when Sanguine Pool is down, and by whether Grievous Wounds is on him before extended trades.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Sanguine Pool 28s->16s, Transfusion 9s->4.6s and Lux's W/R; the do's and don'ts bodies now state the 600-versus-1100 range gap and the health-cost trading.

audit.why: The most punishable cooldown in this matchup is a number — Sanguine Pool at 28s rank 1 is a 26-second window where he has no escape at all.
report[8].t already says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', which is the correct answer to the needs-antiheal interaction; I reinforced it in the ahead field rather than duplicating it.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d were bodies that did not answer their titles, and dontsFull[0].d used 'they' for a single male enemy. report[10].t contained 'ping your jungler every Mantra' — Mantra is Karma's mechanic, a leak from another champion's page.
audit.why: Each is a template or a bleed, not a fact about this matchup.
audit.corrected: All six bullet bodies rewritten to match their titles and grounded in Vladimir's ranges and cooldowns; the Mantra reference replaced with Final Spark's 60-second cycle.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Prismatic Barrier for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — 2 seconds untargetable eats your whole combo, so bait it and commit in the 20+ seconds after. - Transfusion is 9s at rank 1 but 4.6s maxed: his sustain doubles as he levels it. - Your W is 12s, R 60s.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Tides of Blood and Transfusion both stop at 600, so E his farm spot from 1100 and he pays health or gives up CS.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Every spell charges Illumination; the follow-up auto ignites it for bonus magic damage, so take one auto after each E detonation.

edits.before: Vladimir spends Sanguine Pool early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Root him the moment he steps to 600 for Transfusion — no dash means the binding is unavoidable.

edits.before: That’s Vladimir’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Q is 10 seconds and 50 mana; miss it and he walks in with your only lockdown gone.

edits.before: Your W answers exactly one combo per fight — shield the spell that kills, not the one that stings.
edits.after: Tides of Blood costs him health, not mana, so he throws it forever — stay outside 600 while your E is down.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60 seconds at rank 1 — spend it on the wave and the next fight starts with Hemoplague up and your answer down.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by surviving the early game, then letting Crimson Pact turn health items into AP until your poke heals off.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Vladimir off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, keep him under tower: his only escape is a 28-second pool, so root the moment it is spent, buy anti-heal early, and never let him farm back to his items.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by killing him before Crimson Pact does its work — 1175 root into Q-E-R while his health pool is small; after two items he outlasts the combo.

edits.before: Best wave: an E-cleared slow push that crashes on your roam-or-recall timer — the slow zone makes the crash safe to set up. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with Q down — the immobile root-bot walking up to farm is mid's most quoted death. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: an E-cleared slow push crashed on your recall timer — he clears with Tides of Blood at 600, so make him step into your 1100 to do it. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with Q down, where Transfusion tops him up off every minion you leave. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam.

edits.before: If Vladimir takes first blood, tighten up: Sanguine Pool is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: If Vladimir takes first blood, tighten up: every gold he gets becomes health and health becomes AP through Crimson Pact. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn't — E-farm and play for root picks.

edits.before: Chip with E and the passive weave — your poke is honest and your root threat is the law. Bank Manaflow; the laser runs on it.
edits.after: Chip with E from 1100 and weave the Illumination auto — Transfusion needs 600, so every heal he takes off you costs a step forward.

edits.before: Luden's onward, every root is a kill: shove, hover the river, and Q-R the first contest. Your range decides objective setups alone.
edits.after: Luden's onward you are racing his sustain: shove, roam, and take fights where anti-heal is already applied — extended trades belong to him.

edits.before: Lost Chapter steadies the chip; level 6 turns roots into kills; Luden's makes Q-E-R a deletion.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies mana; 6 turns roots into kills; his first item is when your poke stops sticking.

edits.before: You are the longest 'no' in the game: root the engage, slow the pit, and laser whatever your team's front line holds still.
edits.after: Late he dives your backline out of the pool, so hold Q for his landing and let anti-heal, not damage, decide whether he lives.

edits.before: Q-E on arrival is a guaranteed gank: root, slow, detonate. Post-6 your R cleans the Flash they burn — ping your jungler every Mantra... every laser cycle.
edits.after: Q-E on arrival is a guaranteed gank: root, slow, detonate. Post-6 your R cleans the Flash they burn — ping your jungler on every 60-second laser cycle.
